subject: math

objective.text: Subtract with the standard algorithm, regrouping many times, even through zeros. Solve word problems.

explanations.title: Regroup many times
explanations.text: Check every column from right to left. Each column that lacks units needs 1 unit unbundled from its left. You may regroup in many columns.

explanations.title: Regroup through zeros
explanations.text: If a number has zeros, unbundle the first non-zero unit on the left. Pass units down through each zero.

explanations.title: Subtract from 1,000,000
explanations.text: Rename 1,000,000 as 9s in every place and 10 ones. Then every column is ready to subtract.

explanations.title: Check by adding the parts
explanations.text: Add the difference to the part you subtracted. The sum should be the whole.

explanations.title: Tape diagram shows the operation
explanations.text: The tape shows the whole and the parts. If you know the whole and one part, subtract to find the other part.

examples.title: 253,421 minus 75,832
examples.text: Regroup in the ones, tens, hundreds and thousands columns. The answer is 177,589.

examples.title: 1,000 minus 528
examples.text: There are no tens or hundreds to unbundle. Unbundle 1 thousand. Now there are 9 hundreds 9 tens 10 ones. The answer is 472.

examples.title: 1,000,000 minus 345,528
examples.text: Rename 1,000,000 as 9s in every place and 10 ones. The answer is 654,472.

examples.title: Parade attendance
examples.text: 620,073 minus 456,795 is 163,278. There were 163,278 more people last year.

hints.text: Say the digit and its place. Then say its value.
Subtract the matching units. Then write the answer.
Count by 20. Switch to meters at 100 and 200.
Find how many 100s of centimeters there are. Then the centimeters left over.
Find the whole and the part you know. Subtract to find the other part.
Compare the top digit with the bottom digit in this column.
Unbundle 1 unit from the column on the left. It becomes 10 of this unit.
Line up the places. Check each column. Unbundle when a column lacks units.
Add the difference to the part you subtracted. Do you get the whole?

assets_required.description: A vertical subtraction with place value columns up to millions. The child checks each column, unbundles through zero columns, subtracts, and checks by adding.
must_show_exactly: Columns in order: millions, hundred thousands, ten thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens, ones
A top number and a bottom number lined up
A ready check for each column
Unbundling that passes through zero columns, such as 1,000,000 renamed as 9s and 10 ones
A tape diagram with the whole, the known part and a variable
A check row that adds the difference and the known part
assets_required.interaction: Child checks each column, unbundles when a column is not ready, then subtracts and checks by adding.
assets_required.alt_text: A vertical subtraction with unbundling through zeros and a tape diagram.
